title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Dillon Brooks draw inspiration from Canada’s World Cup win
content:
TORONTO — As they get ready to help the Canadian men’s basketball team qualify for the 2027 World Cup, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Dillon Brooks have been dabbling in some soccer.

The pair, along with Atlanta’s Nickeil Alexander-Walker, addressed the media before Canada Basketball summer training camp on Monday morning, saying that they have been watching the Canadian senior men’s soccer team’s unprecedented run to the round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.

Canada beat South Africa 1-0 in the round of 32 on Sunday, the country’s first-ever win in a knockout game. Before this World Cup, the men’s team had never recorded a point in two previous trips to the event, losing all six of their matches. Canada went 1-1-1 in group play before Sunday’s win.

“I’ve been watching their games. Their success has been inspiring,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “To see the growth of their program, where it has come in a short amount of time, the growth of the players, it’s been inspiring. It’s been fun. It makes me proud to be Canadian.”

Canada will play the winner of Monday’s match between Morocco and the Netherlands.

“It’s been great. I went to the game in Toronto (against Bosnia-Herzegovina),” Brooks said. “I went to Vancouver. I know they’re probably ecstatic for the success that they’ve had. The support is fully here throughout the whole country no matter what. I can’t wait to see (how) they play in the next round.”

Gilgeous-Alexander and Brooks are two of the biggest names playing for Canada in this window of World Cup qualification in the Americas. They are finishing up the first round of the qualification process with two games in Hamilton, Ont., Gilgeous-Alexander’s hometown. They play Puerto Rico on Friday and Jamaica on July 6.

They will have to put the first round of the playoffs, when Gilgeous-Alexander’s Thunder swept Brooks’ Suns, behind them. Brooks had to guard Gilgeous-Alexander for much of the series, calling him “a little frail” after Game 2. Gilgeous-Alexander put several photos on Instagram after the series, including one of Brooks wearing a jersey that said “Cancun on 3.”

Publicly, both players have been complimentary of one another, although Brooks didn’t hide his frustration on Monday when asked about guarding the two-time MVP.

“I wanted to tackle him,” Brooks said.

“I think he’s very (hard to rattle). That’s why he’s the captain of our team, super composed, knows the game. I will never forget after we lost to France (in the quarterfinals of the Olympics, Rowan (Barrett, the general manager of the Canadian team) told him he’s got to be our leader and lead us to where we need to be. That’s why we’re all here.”

It was an eventful spring for the Canadian duo.

In May, sports prediction market company Underdog created a board game called “Unethical Hoops”, spoofing the classic game “Operation” by making fun of ways the Thunder star draws fouls. Underdog had Brooks appear in a commercial for the game. Underdog said they would not only give away 100 of the games, but also offered $100 to a random fan each time Gilgeous-Alexander fell on a shot attempt in Game 3 of the Western Conference finals.

In the game, there are labels such as “lean in,” “head snap,” “push off” and “phantom foul” that cause the buzzer to go off.

In a letter dated May 22, Eric Fishman of law firm ArentFox Schiff LLP, a lawyer representing Gilgeous-Alexander, asked the company to “permanently cease and desist from any and all use of Mr. Gilgeous-Alexander’s NIL in any and all media,” including the game. As of Monday, the website for the game is still up.

Along with Gilgeous-Alexander, Brooks and Alexander-Walker, Indiana’s Andrew Nembhard and Dallas’ Ryan Nembhard will be available to play for Canada in this window. RJ Barrett, Bennedict Mathurin, Lu Dort and Zach Edey are among the NBA players who are involved with the program but will not play in this window. Earlier in the offseason, Canada Basketball said Denver star Jamal Murray, who played for Canada at the Paris Olympics, will not be a part of the program in this cycle.
